Commissioner(ST).

building , Chennai North Division, Elephant Bridge Road , Vepery Chennai -03 for conducting the

property on the scheduled dates with prior permission from seller by contacting the details
provided in sale notice/auction notice.

the property and no representations and warranties are given by the Seller/MSTC relating to

survey/Municipal/Corporation/Industrial Nos. and respective maps, extent/area of Land,
boundaries, statutory sanctions or approval and all other dues statutory/other with respect to
im

movable property prior to submission of bid in the e-Auction. No dispute in this regard will be
entertained by the Seller/Selling Agency after submission of bids/auction. 
20)  The Bidder will not raise any dispute regarding the terms and conditions of the e-auction or
about the particulars of the scheduled property or contest the same once he has been declared as
successful Bidder. 
21)  Any Bid made shall be deemed to have been submitted after complete satisfaction of the title,
status, condition, quantity and quality etc., of the scheduled property/ies. Conditional offers/bids
shall not be accepted. Amendment to the offers/bids shall not be permitted after the closure of e-
auction. The rule of caveat emptor is applicable. 
22)  Pre-Bid EMD (PEMD): 
1. To deposit Pre-Bid EMD (herein after referred to as PEMD) amount as mentioned in the auction
catalogue or under lot details, a registered bidder has to login and go to Pay Pre-Bid EMD Link in
his home page.

the PEMD amount into MSTC bank account. Therefore, Bidders are advised to make Pre-Bid
EMD payment well in advance of the Auction start date to avoid any last-minute hassles. Seller/
MSTC shall not be responsible for any delay in receipt of Pre-Bid EMD amount. 
3. Each bidder has been assigned a specific Virtual Account number. Same can be re-used by the
bidder any number of times. In case the amount does not reflect in EMD LEDGER after one day, a
mail may be sent toglobalemd@mstcindia.co.in along with attachments of RTGS Slip and UTR
number for verification. Bidders can only participate in e-auction if EMD/PRE BID EMD is credited
in EMD LEDGER. For post auction payments buyer needs contact the seller for making payments
to bank accounts provided by seller. 
4. For successful bidder (Highest bidder) PEMD amount corresponding to the Lot/auction, as
defined in the auction terms, will be blocked and retained with MSTC and will be transferred to
sellers account. 
5. For unsuccessful bidder his PEMD amount will be available in his EMD Ledger for raising
refund. The EMD/PEMD amount is refundable without interest to the unsuccessful bidders who
are not Highest. Refund of the EMD/PRE BID EMD can be initiated by the bidders themselves,
from their login in MSTC Portal, after e-auction, in forenoon of every working day, by clicking on
the button EMD REFUND REQUEST. EMD refund request facility will be enabled for bidders
whose bank details are verified. The same may be checked through My Profile option available in
bidders dashboard. FAQs for Pre-Bid EMD Payment are available on the link Pay Pre-Bid EMD in
the login of Bidder. 
6. Amount of PEMD deposited shall be interest free and

carry no interest under any
circumstances.
7.Forfeiture of Pre-Bid EMD: Since the Pre-Bid EMD is specified on a lot-wise basis, the pre-bid
EMD shall be forfeited for the specific lot in which the successful bidder defaults in the payment of
the post-auction payments i.e., only the Pre-Bid EMD corresponding to that specific lot where the
successful bidder defaults shall be forfeited without any prior notice, if the successful bidder fails to
adhere to the terms of sale.

,BUYER SPECIFIC TERMS & CONDITIONS (BSTC) AND SPECIAL TERMS & CONDITIONS
(STC). MSTC shall have the right to issue addendum to the GTC or BSTC to clarify, amend,
modify, supplement or delete any of the conditions, clauses or items stated therein and the
Addendum so issued shall form a part of the original.

interest free EMD/pre-bid amount on or before one day prior to scheduled date and time as
prescribed above.
25)  The prospective bidders should comply with KYC norms. All financial transaction towards e-
auction sale of scheduled property must be made by the bidder only through the bank account
registered with MSTC.

https://www.mstcecommerce.com/auctionhome/index_new.jsp by clicking on link View Live

with minimum increment as mentioned in sale notice.

MESSAGE on the Bidder s screen before he confirms/submits the bid.

the link "Auction Lot Status" immediately after closing of e-Auction. Highest Bid received will be
submitted to seller for final decision and further action. A system generated automatic Sale
Intimation Letter will be issued by e-mail to the Highest Bidder after closure of e-au

ction. Highest
Bidders must therefore keep a watch on their incoming e-mail. No hard copy of the Sale Intimation
Letter will be issued by MSTC.
32)  Email Address of Bidders must always be kept valid, failing which Bidders will be liable for
non-compliance of instructions required to be issued by Seller/MSTC to them via email.

hosted on webpage for guidance of intending bidders and pertaining to the e-auction sale & Terms

STC displayed under "View Live/Forthcoming Auctions" on MSTC's e-Auction Website are

Bidders should therefore download the details of properties List and STC displayed only under
"View Live Auctions" for their record purpose, if required. Participation in the e-Auction will be
deemed to imply that the Bidders have made themselves thoroughly aware of and accepted the
STC, and List.

to demand the automatic confirmation of sale in his / her favor.

s will be valid for acceptance for

2) The full amount is to be deposited to seller by the successful bidder on 30th day calculated from

e prescribed, failing which the amount

The Punjab Police claim to

manbir Singh Gill said inves-
tigators were probing the
role of gangster Goldy
Dhillon and other gang
members in the conspiracy
behind the killing.

Rural, was traced to Ahmed-
abad after investigators estab-
lished a money trail involving
his brother Amandeep Singh.

16,000 was transferred online
to Amandeep’s account by
persons allegedly linked to
foreign-based criminals. Of
this, Rs 11,000 was transferred
by Amandeep to Parminder,
while Rs 5,000 was allegedly
transferred to Paramvir Singh
of Lohian Khas.

already under investigation
when Parminder contacted
him for money. The police
asked Amandeep to send a
QR code to Parminder on the
pretext of making a payment.

the code, his location was
traced and the Ahmedabad
Crime Branch was alerted.

Ahmedabad and arrested

gators confronted him with

an, Amritsar Rural.

sioner, Balraj and Vikas
allegedly conducted a recce

stall to Starbucks.

Ahmedabad and arrested

The birth anniversary of the

founder of Amritsar, Guru
Ram Das, will be observed
twice this year due to the con-
tinuing controversy sur-
rounding the Nanakshahi
calendar, leading to different
Gurpurb dates.
The Pakistan Sikh Gurd-
wara Parbandhak Commit-
tee, which follows the original
Nanakshahi calendar based
on the solar year, will cele-
brate the Gurpurb on Octo-
ber 9 at Gurdwara Janam
Asthan Guru Ram Das Ji in
Lahore’s Chuna Mandi area.
In contrast, the Shiromani
Gurdwara Parbandhak Com-

Sikh Gurdwara Management

commemorate the occasion

the amended Nanakshahi
calendar, which incorporates
lunar calculations and is
endorsed by the Akal Takht.
DSGMC president
Harmeet Singh Kalka said,
“We go by the calendar
endorsed by the Akal Takht.
Accordingly, Guru Ram Das
Ji’s birth anniversary will be
celebrated on October 27.”
The differing dates have
once again highlighted the
long-standing divide in the
Sikh community over the
Nanakshahi calendar. 
Several Sikh organisations
in India and abroad, includ-
ing Panthic Talmel Sangath-
an, Akal Purakh Ki Fauj and
Shabad Kirtani Jatha, have
aligned with Sikhs in Pak-
istan and will observe the
Gurpurb on October 9.
Jaswinder Singh Advocate,
head of Akal Purakh Ki Fauj,
blamed the SGPC for the con-
fusion, alleging that amend-
ments to the original
Nanakshahi calendar had
altered its character. “The
original calendar was modi-
fied for political reasons. As a
result, confusion persists
over the dates of Gurpurbs
and other significant Sikh
occasions,” he said.
Disputes over the calen-
dar have resurfaced repeat-
edly since the amendments
were introduced in 2010.
Critics often describe the
amended version as a
return to the Bikrami cal-
endar system under the
Nanakshahi nomenclature
because it incorporates
lunar calculations.
